gui.dysoncubeproject.cosmic_mining.toolt: The planet type represents this tier's resource weighting. An unmined target is a deterministic preview and is not added to global target data until mining starts.
Total target mass is controlled by its tier, stored as an exact BigDecimal string, and reduced by actual output. The next target unlocks at zero.
A descriptive resource abundance parameter for this planet type. Cosmic progression multipliers do not affect finite matter.
The hub pauses when stopped manually, without energy, or when the planet is depleted. Product buffers use Flux's exact AbsoluteInteger ledger.
The same global BigNumber cache shown by the Dyson Universe Hub. Mining consumes this real Dyson energy balance first.
Combined direct mining-hub input and adjacent laser-port energy. It supplies only the shortfall after the Dyson cache and accepts Flux BigNumber, Flux long, and standard FE input.
Runtime cost is 1000 FE/t multiplied by the selected tier. The complete deduction path uses Flux BigNumber.
An independent 16-level scale for the mining hub. It is separate from Dyson progression and can only be changed before mining starts.

Measured in Earth masses. Levels 1-15 and the default Star End target sample within their tier ranges. Manual Star End mass has a 1E118 M⊕ minimum and no gameplay maximum, stored as an exact finite BigDecimal.
Lv.1 starts at x1 and every level multiplies consumption by 10, reaching x10^15 at Lv.16.
Actual per-tick cost. Dyson global energy is consumed first, then the hub buffer, then adjacent laser input ports.

Star End only. Enter an exact mass of at least 1E118 M⊕ using decimal or scientific notation, with no maximum. It is converted to kilograms and stored with BigDecimal precision, then locked when mining starts.
The exact decimal order of magnitude from Flux BigNumber. Very large scientific exponents remain compact and are never expanded.
Each order of magnitude loses 0.1%% efficiency, with a minimum of 0.1%%. Calculation uses Flux BigNumber throughout.
The BigNumber laser input is converted and limited by remaining planetary mass before its integer output enters the Flux AbsoluteInteger ledger.
Output relative to laser input 1. Products are stored in a dynamically growing Flux AbsoluteInteger ledger.
Water, lava, and detected technology-mod gases use an exact Flux AbsoluteInteger mB ledger and are projected into finite batches for ordinary pipes and AE-compatible interfaces.
